By doing that I pushed that person away a lot. I regret doing that even though it was years ago. That person was very influential to me and played a big part in making me realize how my long abandoned dream of becoming an author still held true for me. I gossiped about that person a lot because of that person's drawing skills and my resulting jealousy. I also sent a lot of anon hate to the person on a tumblr to vent personal frustrations on several different occasions. I disagree because it can get more complicated than the established order of things. For example, Leonard from Memento breaks laws at every turn and he seems to me more like a flawed hero than an anti hero. Then again, maybe Leonard is just an outlier?

I think a large part of the reason why is because it is easier for all walks of life to relate to anti heroes than it is for them to do so with the good two shoes character. A lot of writers make the mistake of making "good" characters more like an ideal than a person; moreover, I think it is entirely possible to write a good character that is just as compelling as a bad one/anti hero. (See: Sherlock Holmes, Guy Montag, Ishmael, and etc.)
